disclaimer: TrustScore is a demonstration of responsible-AI credit decisioning. It is not a real lending tool, not financial advice, and not a loan offer. Decisions shown are simulated.

role_split.train: fit booster + cross-fitted isotonic calibration + equalized-odds mitigation
role_split.validation: policy verification and the interactive auditor *policy tuning* set
role_split.test: one-time held-out final evaluation (model card, evaluation report)

policy_tuning_set.name: validation
policy_tuning_set.note: The auditor console experiments only on this set.

final_evaluation_set.name: test
final_evaluation_set.note: Row-level test data is never shipped, so it stays held out.

grid_verification.note: Search only. A zero delta means the surface is flat across a gap in the score distribution, so the grid point is arbitrary.

cost_matrix.units: cost per unit of loan amount (exposure)

definitions.disparate_impact_ratio: min/max selection rate across adequately-sized groups; the 'four-fifths rule' flags a ratio below 0.80
definitions.equalized_odds_difference: max(TPR gap, FPR gap) across adequately-sized groups

uncertainty.method: Wilson score interval for rates; percentile bootstrap for disparity ratios
uncertainty.note: Intervals are sampling uncertainty only. They do not cover dataset, group-definition or metric-choice uncertainty.

fairness.disclaimer: This dashboard reports statistical disparities between groups. It does not establish legal compliance or non-compliance, and it is not a legal opinion.

guardrail.interpretation: A ratio at or above the floor for one attribute is not evidence that the system is fair overall, and it is not a legal-compliance finding. Every remaining breach is listed here and must be read together with its confidence interval and its group sizes.

ablation.reason: loan_grade is assigned by the lender at origination and loan_int_rate follows from it, so both encode the lender's own underwriting judgement rather than an independent applicant signal.
ablation.evaluated_on: test (both rows uncalibrated and on the same split)
ablation.provenance_note: Both rows are uncalibrated and evaluated on the same test split, so the delta is like-for-like. It measures how much of the headline ranking skill came from reproducing the lender's own risk tiering; a system that must score applicants the lender has not already judged should expect the lower number.

income_segment_holdout.note: The dataset has no timestamp, so a temporal split is not possible. Holding out an entire income segment is the closest available proxy: it shows how ranking skill changes on applicants drawn from a part of the population the model never trained on. The random stratified split used for the headline metrics does not capture this.

metric_definitions.pr_auc: Average precision; more informative than ROC-AUC when defaults are rare.
metric_definitions.brier: Mean squared error of the predicted probabilities; lower is better.
metric_definitions.ece: Expected calibration error across 10 probability bins; lower is better.
metric_definitions.selection_rate: Share of a group that is approved.
metric_definitions.tpr: P(approved | repaid) — approval rate among the creditworthy.

limitations: Trained on the public Kaggle Credit Risk Dataset, which is not Nigerian credit data. It demonstrates the system, not a production score for any real market.

Fairness is audited only for attributes present in the data (home ownership, age band, income band, loan purpose, prior default flag). Gender, race/ethnicity, geography and other attributes are not in the dataset and are reported as 'not available'.
Fairness figures are statistical disparities between groups. They do not prove legal compliance or non-compliance.
Counterfactuals are model-generated scenarios, not guaranteed approval conditions.
Performance monitoring is offline/simulated: the public dataset has no live outcome stream.
Deployment targets a serverless environment, so the production model is kept deliberately light (LightGBM only; no SHAP library at runtime).

The measured ROC-AUC is optimistic for a real credit setting: the dataset's loan grade and interest rate are lender-assigned fields that already encode an underwriting judgement, so part of the model's skill is reproducing the lender's own risk tiering rather than independent prediction.

All headline metrics come from a single random stratified split of one public dataset. A random split measures performance on a similar distribution; it does not establish performance on future applicants or on a different population. The out-of-population check in this card exists precisely because the random split hides the difference.

The auditor console runs only on the validation (policy tuning) split. Its live figures are therefore not the published test figures, and it must not be used to select a policy on the basis of test-set performance.

Fairness mitigation is an experimental policy intervention, not a fairness guarantee and not a legal-compliance finding. It targets one attribute at a time; other audited attributes can and do remain below the four-fifths floor with it enabled.

drift.method: Population Stability Index (decile bins for numerics)
drift.note: Offline/simulated: the public dataset has no live outcome stream, so this compares the training split (reference) with the held-out test split (current).
